summary: Macro inheritance causing SLA weight conflicts during routing rollout
description:
Issue summary: During a staged rollout of a new routing macro bundle, we observed conflicting SLA weight assignments inherited by child routing profiles. Impact: A subset of internal support routes were deprioritized unexpectedly, resulting in delayed automated triage and increased manual reassignments (~12% increase in median time-to-first-action for affected queues over the rollout window).

Observed behavior: The macro bundle 'support/sla_v2' contains a top-level SLA weight of 10 with an override rule for 'priority:internal' to 8. When the bundle was applied, several downstream routing profiles (created via inheritance templates) ended up with weight=0 in the active routing table due to an incorrect merge that treated missing keys as explicit zeroes. Expected behavior: Inherited routing profiles should inherit numeric SLA weights from parents unless explicitly overridden; missing fields should not be treated as zero.

Why this matters: SLA weight drives our automated routing and prioritization in the support router. Incorrect zeroing caused lower-priority buckets to consume less capacity than expected and pushed tickets to manual queues. This rollout impacted internal SLAs tied to response SLAs for P1/P2 internal tickets, and temporarily broke some autoscaling decisions made by the sla-orchestrator.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a macro bundle 'support/sla_v2' with top-level 'sla.weight: 10' and an override 'match: {priority: internal} -> sla.weight: 8'
2) Create a child routing profile via inheritance that does not explicitly define 'sla.weight'
3) Deploy the macro bundle with the routing-engine preview and apply to staging routing table
4) Observe the active routing table entries for the child profile showing 'sla.weight: 0' and compare to expected '8 or 10',
5) Reproduce by applying to a small subset of prod namespaces (we did this for 'support-team-alpha') and watch triage throughput drop
logs:
[2026-03-05T14:02:13Z] router.apply: bundle=support/sla_v2; result=ok
[2026-03-05T14:02:14Z] routing-engine: profile=alpha-internal; sla.weight=0; source=merge_step
[2026-03-05T14:05:01Z] sla-orchestrator: allocated-concurrency=2 -> expected=6; decision=deprioritize
[2026-03-05T15:12:44Z] support-ops-alert: increased-mtfa=12pct; bucket=internal-alpha
(see attached logs in internal S3: s3://redwood-support/logs/2026-03-05/INT-47321/merge-debug.log)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: merge function treats undefined keys as default 0 for numeric fields. Verified by running unit tests for merge logic on schema v3.
Reproduction in staging: toggling 'treat_missing_as_none' flag in router preview produces correct behavior; when flag is false, missing numeric field becomes 0.

Root cause: a change in the routing-engine merge library (commit 9f7a2c) changed the default for NumberNode.merge() to coerce null->0 for backward compatibility with legacy routes. That change did not account for macro inheritance semantics.
Scope: 7 routing profiles in prod were affected during the rollout window; historical runs show this merge behavior is new as of 2026-02-28 deployments.
Risk: Applying a hotfix to the merge library can affect other systems that expected the coercion; need careful rollout and compatibility tests.
comments: 2026-03-05 Priya Desai: Reported spike in manual triage after macro rollout; created ticket and attached initial logs.
2026-03-05 Marco Alvarez: Reproduced in staging and confirmed 'sla.weight' zeroing. Tentatively marking as merge-library regression — adding sla-orchestrator and routing-engine owners.

2026-03-06 SRE (Lina Park): We can apply a runtime feature flag 'merge_strict_nulls=true' to routing-engine nodes in prod to restore previous behavior while we prepare a patch. Planning to toggle on a single canary node first.

2026-03-07 Product (Omar Reyes): Noted this affects internal SLAs for feature rollout automation. Requested a short postmortem and add a guardrail in console UI to preview effective SLA weights before applying macro bundles.

2026-03-10 Marco Alvarez: Implemented hotfix branch 'fix/merge-null-coercion' and test harness. Deploy plan: feature flag -> patch to merge library -> gradual rollout across prod routing-engine pods over 3 days. Will document in linked PR.
resolution: Workaround applied: feature-flag 'merge_strict_nulls=true' enabled on canary routing-engine pods which prevented zeroing of missing SLA weights. Hotfix branch prepared and tests added. Full patch pending staged rollout; no full resolution until patch is in prod across all regions.
follow_up_actions: 1) Merge and release fix/merge-null-coercion; run compatibility suite with legacy macro bundles (owner: Marco)
2) Add console preview guardrail that computes effective SLA weights for a bundle before apply (owner: Product/Console)
3) Create telemetry for merge events that log when numeric fields are coerced (owner: Observability)
4) Postmortem documenting timeline and a new playbook for macro rollbacks (owner: Support Ops)
5) Re-audit other merge library uses to ensure no additional accidental coercions (owner: Platform Infra)
6) Communicate to internal teams and suspend broad macro rollouts until patch is in all prod regions (owner: Support Lead)
